chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Khayrānī, from his father, who said:
I was standing before Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام in Khurāsān, when someone said to him, "O my master, if an event should occur, then to whom [shall we turn]?" He said, "To Abī Jaʿfar, my son."

Then it was as though the questioner considered the age of Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام too small, so Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said, "Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent ʿĪsā ibn Maryam عليه السلام as a Messenger, a Prophet, and the possessor of an initiated law, at an age younger than that in which Abū Jaʿfar is."

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ: Abū al-Ḥasan, the Imam عليه السلام being addressed in the report
key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abū Jaʿfar, the son designated as successor
key_terms.اسْتَصْغَرَ: regarded as too young or considered small in age
key_terms.رَسُولًا: a messenger sent by Allah with divine mission
key_terms.شَرِيعَةٍ مُبْتَدَأَةٍ: an initiated or newly established divine law
key_terms.عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ: Jesus son of Mary عليه السلام, cited as a prophetic example
key_terms.كَوْنٌ: an occurring event, here meaning the Imam’s passing or a decisive occurrence

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the Imamate of a young Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the designation of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام as successor after Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, despite his young age. The Imam عليه السلام answers doubt about youth by citing ʿĪsā ibn Maryam عليه السلام, whom Allah appointed to prophethood at an even younger age. The report highlights that divine authority is determined by Allah, not by customary expectations about age.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Al Kahyrani, from his father who said,

‘I was standing in front of Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> (8<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup> at Khurasan, and a speaker said to him, ‘O my Master<sup>asws</sup>! If there occurs the event (of your<sup>asws</sup> passing away), so to whom (show we look to)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘To Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup>’.

So it was as if the speaker was belittling the age of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>. So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Sent Isa<sup>as</sup> Ibn Maryam<sup>as</sup> as a Rasool<sup>as</sup>, a Prophet<sup>as</sup>, as a owner of a Law, beginning at an age younger than that of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 6. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from al-Khayrani from his father who has said the following. “

Once I was standing in the presence of abu al-Hassan (a.s.) in Khurasan and someone said to him, ‘O my master if something will happen to you to who must we then turn for guidance?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “You must turn for guidance to abu Ja‘far (a.s.), my son.”

The person asking the question seemed to have thought of his (abu Ja‘far (a.s.) age very small. Abu al-Hassan (a.s.) then said, “Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, sent Jesus (a.s.) son of Mary as a Messenger and a prophet being the author of a whole system of law. He began this task in an age much smaller than the age of abu Ja‘far (a.s.).”
